text_blocks.snippet: Yes, vaccination rates for some childhood vaccines have decreased in the U.S. in recent years, particularly among children born during the COVID-19 pandemic. Specifically, research from Johns Hopkins University shows a national decline in the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination rate. Similarly, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported declines in coverage for nearly all routinely recommended childhood vaccines among children born in 2020 and 2021 compared to those born in 2018 and 2019.
